answers.question: What should it have?
answers.answer: My name and a short intro, My hobbies

title: A page about me
summary: You'll build a warm, friendly one-page website with your name, a short intro about yourself and a list of your hobbies.
outcome: A finished personal web page that opens in your browser straight from your project folder.

simpler.title: Just a hello and an about-me
simpler.why: Get a real, styled page about you up quickly, then add hobbies, a footer and cards once the basics feel easy.

files.content:
😊

Hi, I'm Sam!

About me

I love learning new things, drinking hot cocoa and spending time with friends. This is my very own little corner of the web.

My hobbies

  • 📚 Reading stories
  • 🎨 Drawing and painting
  • 🚲 Riding my bike
  • 🍪 Baking cookies

Made with ❤️ by Sam

steps.title: Build the page skeleton
steps.instruction: Make a new file called index.html. At the very top, type <!DOCTYPE html>. Under it, add an html tag that opens and closes. Inside it, add a head part (opens and closes), then a body part (opens and closes).
steps.why: Every web page needs this frame: html wraps the whole page, head holds hidden info, and body holds everything people see.

checks.say: I can't find your index.html file yet.
Something in your page frame looks unfinished. Check every tag that opens also closes.
I can't see the head part and the body part inside your html tags yet.
checks.question: Does the file contain an opening and closing html tag with a head section and a body section written inside it?

hints: A page is like a box with two rooms inside: one for hidden info and one for what people see.
Start with <!DOCTYPE html>, then type the html tag. Inside it put head, then body. Each one opens with <name> and closes with </name>.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
…
<body>
…
</html>

concept.title: Tags
concept.explain: Tags are words in angle brackets that tell the browser what each part is; most come in an opening and closing pair.
concept.imageQuery: basic html page structure diagram head body

steps.title: Give the page a name
steps.instruction: Inside the head, add three lines: a meta tag with charset="utf-8", a title tag with the words About Me, and a link tag with rel="stylesheet" and href="style.css".
steps.why: meta lets emojis and accents show properly, title names the browser tab, and link will connect your style file later.

checks.say: I can't see the line that helps emojis show properly yet.
Your page doesn't have a tab name yet.
I can't see the line that connects your style file yet.
checks.name: href

hints: The hidden part of the page needs three bits of info: the letter type, the tab name and a link to a style file.
Inside <head>, type a meta tag with charset="utf-8", a title tag, and a link tag with rel="stylesheet" href="style.css".

<meta charset="…">
<title>…</title>
<link rel="…" href="…">

concept.title: The head
concept.explain: The head holds information about the page, like its tab name, that visitors don't see on the page itself.

steps.title: Say hello
steps.instruction: Inside the body, add a header. In it, put a p (paragraph) with class="avatar" holding a smiley emoji 😊, then an h1 big heading saying Hi, I'm and your name.
steps.why: header is the top part of your page, h1 is the biggest heading, and p holds a piece of text.

checks.say: I can't see your big hello heading at the top yet.
I can't see your smiley at the top yet. Did you give it the name avatar?

hints: Make a top section with a smiley and a big greeting with your name.

concept.title: Headings and paragraphs
concept.explain: h1 is the biggest title on a page, and p is a normal paragraph of text.

steps.title: Write about yourself
steps.instruction: Under the header, add a section. Inside it, put an h2 heading saying About me and a paragraph with a sentence or two about you.
steps.why: A section groups related things together, and h2 is a smaller heading for each part.
steps.expected:
About me

I love learning new things, drinking hot cocoa and spending time with friends. This is my very own little corner of the web.

checks.say: I can't see your About me part with its heading yet.
Your About me part needs a few words about you.

hints: Add a new part below the greeting with a small heading and a few words about you.

concept.title: Sections
concept.explain: A section is a box that groups one topic of your page, like a chapter in a book.

steps.title: List your hobbies
steps.instruction: Under your About me section, add a second section with an h2 saying My hobbies. Under the heading, add a ul list with 4 li items, one hobby each (start each with an emoji if you like).
steps.why: ul makes a bullet list and each li is one item in it.
steps.expected:
My hobbies

  • 📚 Reading stories
  • 🎨 Drawing and painting
  • 🚲 Riding my bike
  • 🍪 Baking cookies

checks.say: I can't see your list of hobbies yet.
Your hobby list should have 4 hobbies.
You need a second part with its own heading for your hobbies.

hints: Make another part like About me, but this time with a bullet list of things you love doing.
After the first </section>, type a new <section> with an <h2>. Under it, a <ul> holding four <li> lines. Close the ul and the section.

concept.title: Lists
concept.explain: ul makes a bullet list, and every li inside it is one bullet point.

steps.title: Sign your page
steps.instruction: Under the hobbies section, add a footer with a paragraph saying Made with ❤️ by and your name.
steps.why: footer is the bottom strip of a page, a nice place to sign your work.

concept.title: Footers
concept.explain: A footer is the bottom part of a page, often used for a signature or small notes.

steps.title: See your page
steps.instruction: Open index.html in your web browser (double-click it). You'll see your words, plain and simple. Next we'll add colour!
steps.why: Seeing your work in the browser shows that your code really makes a page.
hints: Find index.html in your folder.
Double-click it, or drag it into a browser window.
If it opens in your editor instead, right-click it and choose to open it with your browser.

quiz.question: Which tag makes one item in a bullet list?
quiz.explain: li is one list item; ul is the whole list around them.

steps.title: Colour the background
steps.instruction: Make a new file called style.css. Type a rule for body that sets background to #fff4e6 and color to #5a3e2b.
steps.why: background paints behind your page, and color sets the colour of the text.

checks.say: I can't find your style.css file yet.
Your page background isn't a warm cream colour yet.
Your text isn't brown yet.

hints: Tell the whole page what colour to be behind, and what colour its words should be.
In style.css write body, then curly brackets. Inside: background: #fff4e6; and color: #5a3e2b;

concept.title: CSS rules
concept.explain: CSS picks a part of your page, then lists how it should look inside curly brackets.

steps.title: Choose a font and spacing
steps.instruction: Inside your body rule, under the color line, add font-family: Georgia, serif; then margin: 0; then padding: 20px;
steps.why: font-family picks the letter style, margin is the space outside a box, and padding is the space inside it.

checks.say: Your letters haven't changed to the Georgia style yet.
Your page still has the browser's own gap around the edge.
I can't see the comfy space inside your page edge yet.

hints: Give the page a friendlier letter style and some breathing room inside the edges.
Under the color line, add font-family with Georgia, serif, then margin set to 0, then padding set to 20px.

concept.title: Margin and padding
concept.explain: Padding is the space inside a box around its content; margin is the space outside, pushing other things away.
concept.imageQuery: css box model margin padding diagram

steps.title: Centre the greeting
steps.instruction: Under the body rule, add a header rule with text-align: center; Then add a rule for .avatar with font-size: 64px; and margin: 0;
steps.why: text-align centres the words, and font-size makes your smiley big.

checks.say: Your greeting isn't in the middle yet.
Your smiley isn't big yet.

hints: Put the top part in the middle and make the smiley really big.
Write a header rule with text-align: center; then a .avatar rule (with the dot) with font-size: 64px; and margin: 0;

concept.title: Classes
concept.explain: A dot before a name, like .avatar, styles only the parts you gave that class name.

steps.title: Colour the headings
steps.instruction: Under the .avatar rule, add an h1 rule with color: #d9534f; and font-size: 40px; then an h2 rule with color: #e07b39;
steps.why: Bright headings make your page warm and easy to scan.

checks.say: Your big heading isn't red yet.
Your big heading isn't the new size yet.
Your smaller headings aren't orange yet.

hints: Give your big heading and your smaller headings their own colours.
Write an h1 rule with color #d9534f and font-size 40px, then an h2 rule with color #e07b39.

quiz.question: What does padding do?
quiz.explain: Padding is the space inside a box; margin is the space outside it.

steps.title: Turn sections into cards
steps.instruction: Under the h2 rule, add a section rule with background: #ffffff; and border: 2px solid #f4c095;
steps.why: border draws a line around a box, so each section looks like a white card.

checks.say: Your sections don't have a white background yet.
Your sections don't have a solid line around them yet.
The line around your sections isn't the soft orange colour #f4c095 yet.

hints: Make each part of your page look like a white card with an outline.
Write a section rule with background #ffffff and border set to 2px solid #f4c095.

concept.title: Borders
concept.explain: A border is a line around a box; you choose how thick it is, its style and its colour.

steps.title: Round and centre the cards
steps.instruction: Inside the section rule, under the border line, add border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px; margin: 20px auto; and max-width: 500px;
steps.why: border-radius rounds the corners, max-width stops cards getting too wide, and margin auto centres them.

checks.say: Your cards still have sharp corners.
Your cards can still stretch too wide.
Your cards need some space inside them.

hints: Round the card corners, give them room inside, and keep them a nice width in the middle.
Under the border line add border-radius 16px, padding 20px, margin 20px auto, and max-width 500px.

concept.title: Rounded corners and width
concept.explain: border-radius rounds a box's corners, and max-width sets how wide a box may grow.

steps.title: Tidy the list and footer
steps.instruction: Under the section rule, add an li rule with font-size: 18px; and margin: 8px 0; then a footer rule with text-align: center; and font-size: 14px;
steps.why: Bigger, spaced-out hobbies are easier to read, and a small centred footer looks neat.

checks.say: Your hobbies aren't a bit bigger yet.
Your signature isn't small and centred yet.
Your signature isn't in the middle yet.

hints: Make each hobby a little bigger with space between, and make the signature small and centred.
Write an li rule with font-size 18px and margin 8px 0, then a footer rule with text-align center and font-size 14px.

steps.title: Admire your page
steps.instruction: Go back to your browser and refresh index.html. Your warm, friendly page is finished!
steps.why: Refreshing shows all your colours and cards together.
hints: Find the browser tab with your page.
Press the refresh button or F5.
If nothing changed, check both files are saved and in the same folder.

quiz.question: Which line makes the corners of a box round?
quiz.explain: border-radius controls how rounded the corners are.
